assessments.name: Assessment 3 – Participation and Peer Contribution
assessments.description: This mark recognises your ongoing presence, energy, and artistic generosity in class. It reflects not only your technical preparation but also your mindset, interpersonal integration, and creative courage throughout the semester.
assessments.type: In-person practical, skills, or performance task or test

assessments.name: Early Feedback Task - short improvisation exercise
assessments.description: Improvise a very short solo piano piece, using one of the following approaches: prepared using material of the student's own choosing, based on given material (provided by the teacher), or fully improvised.
assessments.type: In-person practical, skills, or performance task or test

assessments.name: Assessment 1A – Improvised Performance 1
assessments.description: Perform a short solo improvisation that draws on ideas covered in Weeks 1–4, including musical risk-taking, limitation-based improvisation, motivic development, and melodic elaboration.
assessments.type: In-person practical, skills, or performance task or test

assessments.name: Assessment 1B - Improvised Performance 2
assessments.description: Prepare a short solo or duo/ensemble improvisation that draws from the approaches introduced in Weeks 5–8, including rhythmic play, working with lead sheets, harmonising and reharmonising known melodies, and interpreting graphic or text-based scores.
assessments.type: In-person practical, skills, or performance task or test

assessments.name: Assessment 1C - Improvised Performance 3
assessments.description: Solo (optional collaborative) improvisation drawing from any material this semester. Emphasis on: narrative flow, spontaneous form, and ensemble awareness, and artistic voice through thoughtful integration of techniques and ideally, original approaches.
assessments.type: In-person practical, skills, or performance task or test

assessments.name: Assessment 2 – Weekly Reflections on Discussion Board
assessments.description: Weekly written reflections. To be posted to the discussion board by 11:59pm the evening before class. Reflections should address the student's own creative development and the content covered in class, and must be posted even in weeks a class is missed.
